theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_iff_wordRule
theorems.claim: the executable step agrees exactly with one independent rule per word stated from the fragment prose
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_iff_wordRule : ∀ (word : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word) (operands out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.step word operands = some out ↔ NobleFoundation.Ownership.WordRule word operands out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.judged_iff_accounts
theorems.claim: the judgment built on the independent per-word rules coincides with Accounts
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.judged_iff_accounts : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program) (start out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program start out ↔ NobleFoundation.Ownership.Accounts program start out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_complete
theorems.claim: every Accounts derivation is a checker acceptance
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_complete : ∀ {program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program} {start out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Accounts program start out → NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program start = some out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_iff_judged
theorems.claim: the checker decides the independent judgment exactly
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_iff_judged : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program) (start out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program start = some out ↔ NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program start out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_preserves_agreement
theorems.claim: one step preserves eligibility agreement on the stacks it admits in both arms
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_preserves_agreement : ∀ (word : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word) {left right left' right' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → NobleFoundation.Ownership.step word left = some left' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.step word right = some right' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_sequence_admission_agrees
theorems.claim: on a straight-line program two eligibility-agreeing stacks are admitted in both arms or neither and leave agreeing stacks
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_sequence_admission_agrees : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program), NobleFoundation.Ownership.StraightLine program → ∀ (left right : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program left).isSome = (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program right).isSome ∧ ∀ (left' right' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program left = some left' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program right = some right' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_judgment_transfers
theorems.claim: a straight-line judgment carries over to any eligibility-agreeing start with agreeing results
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_judgment_transfers : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program), NobleFoundation.Ownership.StraightLine program → ∀ {left right left' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program left left' → ∃ right', NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program right right' ∧ NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.equal_length_does_not_lift
theorems.claim: equal-length stacks that disagree on eligibility separate a straight-line dup
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.equal_length_does_not_lift : [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1].length = [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1].length ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1]).isSome = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1]).isSome = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.lift_fixture
theorems.claim: stacks with different owners but agreeing eligibility run a three-word sequence alike and agree again
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.lift_fixture : NobleFoundation.Ownership.run ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.swap).compose ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup).compose (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.drop))) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2] = some [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1] ∧ NobleFoundation.Ownership.run ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.swap).compose ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup).compose (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.drop))) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 9, (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 3).wrapped] = some [(NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 3).wrapped, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 9] ∧ NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1] [(NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 3).wrapped, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 9]

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.agreement_length
theorems.claim: stacks that agree on eligibility have the same length
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.Ownership.agreement_length : ∀ {left right : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → left.length = right.length

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.accepted_results_agree
theorems.claim: for every program, branches and the error return included, two admitted runs from eligibility-agreeing stacks leave agreeing stacks
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.accepted_results_agree : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program) (left right left' right' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program left = some left' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program right = some right' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.branch_free_admission_agrees
theorems.claim: on every branch-free program, the error return included, eligibility-agreeing stacks are admitted alike
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.branch_free_admission_agrees : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program), NobleFoundation.Ownership.BranchFree program → ∀ (left right : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program left).isSome = (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program right).isSome

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.branch_admission_does_not_lift
theorems.claim: a branch between swap and dup; drop is admitted on [data 1, data 1] and refused on the eligibility-agreeing [data 1, data 2]
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.branch_admission_does_not_lift : NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1] [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2] ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.swap).branch ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup).compose (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.drop))) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1]).isSome = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.swap).branch ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup).compose (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.drop))) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2]).isSome = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.fail_admission_lifts
theorems.claim: the error return is admitted exactly on the empty stack
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.fail_admission_lifts : (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.fail []).isSome = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.fail [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1]).isSome = false ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.fail [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1]).isSome = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.judged_results_agree
theorems.claim: two derivations of one program from eligibility-agreeing stacks end in agreeing stacks
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.judged_results_agree : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program) {left right left' right' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program left left' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program right right' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_le_carried
theorems.claim: the carried exponent is at least the scale exponent
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_le_carried : ∀ (a b : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_upper_le
theorems.claim: for every positive input the numerator is at most 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1) times the denominator
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_upper_le : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → ↑a ≤ 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b + 1) * ↑b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_numerator_bound
theorems.claim: below the normal range the subnormal numerator a * 2^149 is at most 2^23 denominators
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_numerator_bound : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149 ≤ 2 ^ 23 * b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_significand_bound
theorems.claim: below the normal range the rounded subnormal significand is at most 2^23
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_significand_bound : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b ≤ 2 ^ 23

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal
theorems.claim: below the normal range roundPositive is the rounded significand capped at the smallest normal
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal : ∀ (a b : ℕ), (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b = if NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b ≥ NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23 then NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23 else NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_eq_significand
theorems.claim: below the normal range the cap never changes the rounded significand
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_eq_significand : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: a significand below 2^23 encodes the subnormal n * 2^-149
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_scaledMagnitude : ∀ n < 2 ^ 23, NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) = (n, -149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.smallest_normal_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: the significand 2^23 encodes the smallest normal with value 2^23 * 2^-149
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.smallest_normal_scaledMagnitude : NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude (BitVec.ofNat 32 (2 ^ 23)) = (2 ^ 23, -149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.small_encoding_not_negative
theorems.claim: a significand of at most 2^23 encodes a positive sign
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.small_encoding_not_negative : ∀ n ≤ 2 ^ 23, NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.exactValue_small
theorems.claim: every significand of at most 2^23 encodes exactly n * 2^-149
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.exactValue_small : ∀ n ≤ 2 ^ 23, NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) = ↑n * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal_absolute_error
theorems.claim: below the normal range the encoded result is within 2^-150 of the exact quotient
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal_absolute_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_finite_absolute_error
theorems.claim: every positive input with a finite result is within half the spacing of its binade, 2^(max e -126 - 23)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_finite_absolute_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (max (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b) (-126) - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_rule_applies_below_the_normal_range
theorems.claim: non-vacuity: 1/(3*2^130) rounds to the subnormal significand 174763 within the subnormal bound
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_rule_applies_below_the_normal_range : (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair 1 (3 * 2 ^ 130)).2 < -126 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 1 (3 * 2 ^ 130) = 174763 ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 1 (3 * 2 ^ 130))) - 1 / ↑(3 * 2 ^ 130)| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.rounding_to_the_smallest_normal_attains_the_bound
theorems.claim: a tie halfway below 2^-126 rounds to the smallest normal with error exactly 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.rounding_to_the_smallest_normal_attains_the_bound : (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair (2 ^ 24 - 1) (2 ^ 150)).2 < -126 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive (2 ^ 24 - 1) (2 ^ 150) = 2 ^ 23 ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive (2 ^ 24 - 1) (2 ^ 150))) - ↑(2 ^ 24 - 1) / ↑(2 ^ 150)| = 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_results_are_not_relatively_bounded
theorems.claim: a subnormal result with relative error one third shows the subnormal rule must be absolute
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_results_are_not_relatively_bounded : (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair 3 (2 ^ 151)).2 < -126 ∧ 1 / 2 ^ 24 * (3 / ↑(2 ^ 151)) < |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 3 (2 ^ 151))) - 3 / ↑(2 ^ 151)|

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactValue_eq_scaledValue
theorems.claim: the exact value is the signed scaled integer times its power of two
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactValue_eq_scaledValue : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue b = ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledValue b).1 * 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledValue b).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.toNat_ofNat_of_lt
theorems.claim: a 32-bit encoding of a value below 2^32 keeps the value
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.toNat_ofNat_of_lt : ∀ n < 2 ^ 32, (BitVec.ofNat 32 n).toNat = n

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exponent_of_toNat
theorems.claim: the exponent field is bits 23 to 30
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exponent_of_toNat : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.exponent b = BitVec.toNat b / 2 ^ 23 % 2 ^ 8

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.fraction_of_toNat
theorems.claim: the fraction field is the low 23 bits
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.fraction_of_toNat : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.fraction b = BitVec.toNat b % 2 ^ 23

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.isNegative_of_toNat
theorems.claim: the sign is bit 31
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.isNegative_of_toNat : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative b = (BitVec.toNat b / 2 ^ 31 == 1)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactValue_signed
theorems.claim: setting the sign bit of a magnitude below 2^31 negates its exact value
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactValue_signed : ∀ magnitude < 2 ^ 31, NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (magnitude ||| 2147483648)) = -NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 magnitude)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.pow2Int_pos
theorems.claim: every model power of two is positive
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.pow2Int_pos : ∀ (k : ℤ), 0 < NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2Int k

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs_pos
theorems.claim: a nonzero scaled integer hands roundPositive a positive ratio
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs_pos : ∀ (m s : ℤ), m ≠ 0 → 0 < (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s).1 ∧ 0 < (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs_ratio
theorems.claim: the ratio handed to roundPositive is the magnitude of m times 2^s
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs_ratio : ∀ (m s : ℤ), ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s).1 / ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s).2 = ↑m.natAbs * 2 ^ s

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.carried_significand_lt
theorems.claim: the carried significand stays below 2^24, also on the power boundary
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.carried_significand_lt : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.roundPositive_normal_nat
theorems.claim: in the normal range roundPositive is the normal encoding of the carried pair
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.roundPositive_normal_nat : ∀ (a b : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.InRange (a, b) → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b = ((NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 + 127).toNat * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23 + ((NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).1 - NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.roundPositive_lt
theorems.claim: a normal-range rounding leaves the sign bit clear
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.roundPositive_lt : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.InRange (a, b) → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b < 2 ^ 31

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.roundScaled_relative_error
theorems.claim: rounding a signed scaled integer with its own sign is within 2^-24 of it relatively in the normal range
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.roundScaled_relative_error : ∀ (m s : ℤ), m ≠ 0 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.InRange (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s) → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundScaled m s (decide (m < 0))) - ↑m * 2 ^ s| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |↑m * 2 ^ s|

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactValue_zeroOf
theorems.claim: every signed zero has exact value zero
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactValue_zeroOf : ∀ (negative : Bool), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf negative) = 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.add_eq
theorems.claim: on finite operands add rounds the aligned exact sum once or returns a signed zero
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.add_eq : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.Finite x → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.Finite y → NobleFoundation.Binary32.add x y = if (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.addScaled x y).1 = 0 then NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf (NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative x && NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative y) else NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundScaled (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.addScaled x y).1 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.addScaled x y).2 (decide ((NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.addScaled x y).1 < 0))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.rescale
theorems.claim: moving m times 2^k to a lower scale multiplies the integer by 2^(k - s)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.rescale : ∀ (m k s : ℤ), s ≤ k → ↑m * 2 ^ k = ↑(m * ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2Int (k - s))) * 2 ^ s

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exact_sum
theorems.claim: the aligned integer sum is the exact sum of the two encodings
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exact_sum : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y = ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.addScaled x y).1 * 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.addScaled x y).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.add_relative_error
theorems.claim: one model addition of finite encodings is within 2^-24 of the exact sum relatively when the sum is zero or normal-range
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.add_relative_error : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.AddOk x y → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.add x y) - (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y)| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y|

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exact_product
theorems.claim: the scaled integer product is the exact product of the two encodings
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exact_product : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y = ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).1 * 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.zero_class_magnitude
theorems.claim: a signed zero has magnitude zero
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.zero_class_magnitude : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.posZero ∨ NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.negZero → NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude b = (0, -149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.zero_class_value
theorems.claim: a signed zero has exact value zero
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.zero_class_value : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.posZero ∨ NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.negZero → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue b = 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.nonzero_class_magnitude
theorems.claim: a subnormal or normal encoding has a positive magnitude
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.nonzero_class_magnitude : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.subnormal ∨ NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.normal → 0 < (NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude b).1

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.sign_rule
theorems.claim: a product of two signed positive magnitudes is nonzero and negative exactly when one sign is set
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.sign_rule : ∀ (signX signY : Bool) (mx my : ℕ), 0 < mx → 0 < my → ((if signX = true then -↑mx else ↑mx) * if signY = true then -↑my else ↑my) ≠ 0 ∧ decide (((if signX = true then -↑mx else ↑mx) * if signY = true then -↑my else ↑my) < 0) = (signX != signY)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.product_sign
theorems.claim: the model product of nonzero encodings is nonzero with the XOR sign
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.product_sign : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), 0 < (NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude x).1 → 0 < (NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude y).1 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).1 ≠ 0 ∧ decide ((NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).1 < 0) = (NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative x != NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative y)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mul_scaled_eq
theorems.claim: on two nonzero finite operands mul rounds the exact product once
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mul_scaled_eq : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify x = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.subnormal ∨ NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify x = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.normal → NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify y = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.subnormal ∨ NobleFoundation.Binary32.classify y = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Class.normal → NobleFoundation.Binary32.mul x y = NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundScaled (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).1 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).2 (decide ((NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mulScaled x y).1 < 0))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mul_relative_error
theorems.claim: one model multiplication of finite encodings is within 2^-24 of the exact product relatively when the product is zero or normal-range
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.mul_relative_error : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.MulOk x y → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.mul x y) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y|

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit_nonneg
theorems.claim: the unit roundoff is nonnegative
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit_nonneg : 0 ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.growth_nonneg
theorems.claim: the error growth factor (1 + u)^(2k) - 1 is nonnegative
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.growth_nonneg : ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 ≤ (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * k) - 1

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.step_bound
theorems.claim: one fold step keeps the accumulated error within ((1 + u)^2 (1 + r) - 1) times the grown absolute scale
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.step_bound : ∀ (u r A E a t p v : ℚ), 0 ≤ u → 0 ≤ r → 0 ≤ A → |E| ≤ A → |a - E| ≤ r * A → |p - t| ≤ u * |t| → |v - (a + p)| ≤ u * |a + p| → |v - (E + t)| ≤ ((1 + u) ^ 2 * (1 + r) - 1) * (A + |t|)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.fold_error_from
theorems.claim: the fold from an accumulator within ((1 + u)^(2k) - 1) A of its exact value stays within the grown bound
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.fold_error_from : ∀ (terms : List (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits × NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits)) (accumulator : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits) (E A : ℚ) (k : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.FoldOk accumulator terms → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue accumulator - E| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * k) - 1) * A → |E| ≤ A → 0 ≤ A → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold accumulator terms) - (E + (List.map (fun term => NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.1 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.2) terms).sum)| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * (k + terms.length)) - 1) * (A + (List.map (fun term => |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.1 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.2|) terms).sum)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.fold_error
theorems.claim: the ordered affine fold of n terms is within ((1 + 2^-24)^(2n) - 1) times the bias and term magnitudes of its exact value
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.fold_error : ∀ (bias : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits) (terms : List (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits × NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits)), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.FoldOk bias terms → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold bias terms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine bias terms| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * terms.length) - 1) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale bias terms

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellation_premises
theorems.claim: every premise of the fold bound holds on the documented cancellation fold
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellation_premises : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.FoldOk NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellation_values
theorems.claim: the documented cancellation fold computes +0 for the exact value 1 with absolute scale 1 + 2^25
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellation_values : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms) = 0 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms = 1 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms = 1 + 2 * 2 ^ 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellation_needs_the_term_scale
theorems.claim: the cancellation error 1 is within the fold bound but a bound relative to the exact result alone would be false
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellation_needs_the_term_scale : |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms| = 1 ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms.length) - 1) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms ∧ ¬|NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine NobleFoundation.Binary32.oneBits NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.cancellationTerms|

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta_pos
theorems.claim: half the smallest subnormal spacing is positive
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta_pos : 0 < NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.roundPositive_lt_finite
theorems.claim: a rounding that does not overflow leaves the sign bit clear, including subnormal results
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.roundPositive_lt_finite : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.NoOverflow (a, b) → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b < 2 ^ 31

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.roundPositive_mixed_error
theorems.claim: a positive rounding that does not overflow is within 2^-24 of the ratio relatively plus 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.roundPositive_mixed_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.NoOverflow (a, b) → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * (↑a / ↑b) + NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.roundScaled_mixed_error
theorems.claim: a signed rounding that does not overflow is within 2^-24 relatively plus 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.roundScaled_mixed_error : ∀ (m s : ℤ), m ≠ 0 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.NoOverflow (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s) → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundScaled m s (decide (m < 0))) - ↑m * 2 ^ s| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |↑m * 2 ^ s| + NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.add_mixed_error
theorems.claim: one finite model addition is within 2^-24 of the exact sum relatively plus 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.add_mixed_error : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.AddFinite x y → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.add x y) - (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y)| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y| + NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.mul_mixed_error
theorems.claim: one finite model multiplication is within 2^-24 of the exact product relatively plus 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.mul_mixed_error : ∀ (x y : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.MulFinite x y → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.mul x y) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y| ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit * |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue x * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue y| + NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.step_bound_mixed
theorems.claim: one fold step keeps the relative growth and maps the absolute part H to (1 + u) H + (2 + u) eta
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.step_bound_mixed : ∀ (u r H η A E a t p v : ℚ), 0 ≤ u → 0 ≤ r → 0 ≤ A → |E| ≤ A → |a - E| ≤ r * A + H → |p - t| ≤ u * |t| + η → |v - (a + p)| ≤ u * |a + p| + η → |v - (E + t)| ≤ ((1 + u) ^ 2 * (1 + r) - 1) * (A + |t|) + ((1 + u) * H + (2 + u) * η)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.absolute_growth
theorems.claim: the absolute part after k steps stays below 3k (1 + u)^k eta
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.absolute_growth : ∀ (k : ℕ), (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) * (3 * ↑k * (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ k * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta) + (2 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta ≤ 3 * ↑(k + 1) * (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (k + 1) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.fold_finite_error_from
theorems.claim: the fold from an accumulator within the mixed bound after k steps stays within the grown mixed bound
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.fold_finite_error_from : ∀ (terms : List (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits × NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits)) (accumulator : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits) (E A : ℚ) (k : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.FoldFinite accumulator terms → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue accumulator - E| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * k) - 1) * A + 3 * ↑k * (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ k * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta → |E| ≤ A → 0 ≤ A → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold accumulator terms) - (E + (List.map (fun term => NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.1 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.2) terms).sum)| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * (k + terms.length)) - 1) * (A + (List.map (fun term => |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.1 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue term.2|) terms).sum) + 3 * ↑(k + terms.length) * (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (k + terms.length) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.fold_finite_error
theorems.claim: the ordered affine fold of n terms with no overflow is within the relative bound plus 3n (1 + 2^-24)^n 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.fold_finite_error : ∀ (bias : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits) (terms : List (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits × NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits)), NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.FoldFinite bias terms → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold bias terms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine bias terms| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * terms.length) - 1) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale bias terms + 3 * ↑terms.length * (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ terms.length * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_premises
theorems.claim: the finite premises hold on the subnormal fold
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_premises : NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.FoldFinite (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_fold_is_outside_the_normal_premises
theorems.claim: the normal-range premises of the sequence bound fail on the subnormal fold
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_fold_is_outside_the_normal_premises : ¬NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.FoldOk (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_fold_values
theorems.claim: the subnormal fold computes 2^-148 for the exact value 3 * 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_fold_values : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms) = 2 / 2 ^ 149 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms = 3 / 2 ^ 150 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms = 3 / 2 ^ 150

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_needs_the_absolute_term
theorems.claim: the subnormal fold error 2^-150 is within the finite bound but the relative part alone would be false
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormal_needs_the_absolute_term : |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms| = NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms.length) - 1) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms + 3 * ↑NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms.length * (1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms.length * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.eta ∧ ¬|NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.fold (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms) - NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.exactAffine (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms| ≤ ((1 + NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.unit) ^ (2 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms.length) - 1) * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.affineScale (NobleFoundation.Binary32.zeroOf false) NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.subnormalTerms

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.carried_le_succ
theorems.claim: the carried exponent is at most one above the floor logarithm of the ratio
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.carried_le_succ : ∀ (a b : ℕ), (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b + 1

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.noOverflow_of_lt
theorems.claim: a positive ratio below 2^127 does not overflow
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.noOverflow_of_lt : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → ↑a < NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.overflowLimit * ↑b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.NoOverflow (a, b)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.noOverflow_scaled
theorems.claim: a nonzero m * 2^s of magnitude below 2^127 does not overflow
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.noOverflow_scaled : ∀ (m s : ℤ), m ≠ 0 → |↑m * 2 ^ s| < NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.overflowLimit → NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.NoOverflow (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.scaledArgs m s)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.finite_of_exponent
theorems.claim: an encoding whose exponent field is not all ones is finite
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.finite_of_exponent : ∀ (b : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Bits), NobleFoundation.Binary32.exponent b ≠ 255 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.Finite b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.finite_of_magnitude
theorems.claim: a magnitude below the infinity encoding is finite with either sign
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.finite_of_magnitude : ∀ magnitude < 255 * 2 ^ 23, ∀ (negative : Bool), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Sequence.Finite (BitVec.ofNat 32 (if negative = true then magnitude ||| 2147483648 else magnitude))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.roundPositive_below_infinity
theorems.claim: a positive rounding that does not overflow stays below the infinity encoding
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Checker.roundPositive_below_infinity : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.SequenceFinite.NoOverflow (a, b) → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b < 255 * 2 ^ 23

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.size_le_of_mem
theorems.claim: the instance of a meta is no larger than the instance of a term containing it
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.size_le_of_mem : ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm) {x : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, x ∈ t.vars → (θ x).size ≤ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t).size

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.size_lt_of_mem
theorems.claim: and strictly smaller when the term is not that meta (the occurs-check argument)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.size_lt_of_mem : ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm) {x : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, x ∈ t.vars → t ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.mvar x → (θ x).size < (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t).size

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.subst_single_agree
theorems.claim: binding x := t then applying θ is applying θ whenever θ x is the θ-instance of t
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.subst_single_agree : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, θ x = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t → ∀ (u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) u) = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ u

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.vars_subst_single
theorems.claim: binding x := t removes x and adds at most the metas of t
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.vars_subst_single : ∀ (x : ℕ) (t u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) u).vars ⊆ u.vars.erase x ∪ t.vars

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_skip
theorems.claim: a skipped head equation has identical sides
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_skip : ∀ {s t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.skip → s = t

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_split
theorems.claim: a split head equation equates two applications
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_split : ∀ {s t f g a b : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.split f g a b → s = f.app a ∧ t = g.app b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_bind
theorems.claim: a bound meta passes the occurs check and is one side of the head equation
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_bind : ∀ {s t u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.bind x u → x ∉ u.vars ∧ (s = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.mvar x ∧ t = u ∨ t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.mvar x ∧ s = u)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_cycle
theorems.claim: an occurs failure has no unifier
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_cycle : ∀ {s t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.cycle → ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ s ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_clash
theorems.claim: a clash (different symbols or rigid shapes) has no unifier
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head_clash : ∀ {s t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.clash → ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ s ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unifies_cons
theorems.claim: a unifier of a list unifies its head and its tail
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unifies_cons : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {p : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm × NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ (p :: U) ↔ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ p.1 = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ p.2 ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.satisfies_cons
theorems.claim: a solution of a solved form satisfies its head binding and its tail
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.satisfies_cons : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {q : ℕ × NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ (q :: S) ↔ θ q.1 = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ q.2 ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.mem_eqnVars
theorems.claim: the metas of an equation list are the metas of its equations
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.mem_eqnVars : ∀ {n : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, n ∈ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars U ↔ ∃ p ∈ U, n ∈ p.1.vars ∨ n ∈ p.2.vars

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unifies_substEqns_iff
theorems.claim: binding keeps exactly the unifiers of the remaining equations that agree with it
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unifies_substEqns_iff : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, θ x = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t → ∀ (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substEqns (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) U) ↔ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.satisfies_substSolved_iff
theorems.claim: binding keeps exactly the solutions of the earlier bindings that agree with it
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.satisfies_substSolved_iff : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, θ x = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t → ∀ (S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substSolved (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) S) ↔ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.bind_iff
theorems.claim: a binding step preserves the set of unifiers exactly
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.bind_iff : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, θ x = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S ↔ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substEqns (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) U) ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ ((x, t) :: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substSolved (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) S)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.bind_head_iff
theorems.claim: a bound head equation holds exactly when θ sends the meta to its instance of the other side
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.bind_head_iff : ∀ {s t u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.bind x u → ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ s = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ t ↔ θ x = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ u

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unifies_split
theorems.claim: decomposing two applications preserves the set of unifiers exactly
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unifies_split : ∀ {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {f g a b : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ ((f.app a, g.app b) :: U) ↔ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find_eq_none
theorems.claim: a meta bound by no binding has no lookup
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find_eq_none : ∀ {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {n : ℕ}, (∀ q ∈ S, q.1 ≠ n) → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find S n = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find_of_mem
theorems.claim: with distinct bound metas a binding is what lookup returns
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find_of_mem : ∀ {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, (List.map Prod.fst S).Nodup → ∀ {k : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, (k, t) ∈ S → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find S k = some t

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find_some
theorems.claim: a lookup result is a binding of the solved form
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find_some : ∀ {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {n : ℕ} {t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.find S n = some t → (n, t) ∈ S

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.toSubst_satisfies
theorems.claim: with no equation left the denoted substitution satisfies the solved form
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.toSubst_satisfies : ∀ {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm [] S → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.toSubst S) S

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.toSubst_most_general
theorems.claim: every solution of a solved form factors through the denoted substitution
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.toSubst_most_general : ∀ {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S → ∀ (n : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.toSubst S n) = θ n

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars_cons_subset
theorems.claim: the metas of a tail are metas of the list
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars_cons_subset : ∀ {p : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm × NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars U ⊆ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars (p :: U)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm.tail
theorems.claim: dropping a head equation keeps the solved-form invariant
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm.tail : ∀ {p : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm × NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm (p :: U) S → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm U S

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars_split
theorems.claim: decomposition keeps the metas of the equations
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars_split : ∀ (f g a b : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm) (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U) = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((f.app a, g.app b) :: U)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm.split
theorems.claim: decomposition keeps the solved-form invariant
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm.split : ∀ {f g a b : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm ((f.app a, g.app b) :: U) S → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U) S

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars_substEqns
theorems.claim: binding x := t leaves at most the other metas plus the metas of t
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars_substEqns : ∀ (x : ℕ) (t : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm) (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substEqns (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x t) U) ⊆ (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars U).erase x ∪ t.vars

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm.bind
theorems.claim: a binding step keeps the solved-form invariant
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm.bind : ∀ {s t u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.bind x u → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm ((s, t) :: U) S → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substEqns (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x u) U) ((x, u) :: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substSolved (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x u) S)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_solved
theorems.claim: an answer solved σ unifies the equations and solved form, and every common unifier factors through σ
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_solved : ∀ (fuel : ℕ) {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {σ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U S = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.solved σ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm U S → (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies σ U ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies σ S) ∧ ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S → ∀ (n : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ (σ n) = θ n

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_refused
theorems.claim: a clash or occurs answer means the equations and solved form have no common unifier
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_refused : ∀ (fuel : ℕ) {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U S = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.clash ∨ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U S = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.cycle → ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), ¬(NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.lex_of
theorems.claim: a lexicographic decrease on (metas, size)
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.lex_of : ∀ {a b c d : ℕ}, a < c ∨ a ≤ c ∧ b < d → Prod.Lex (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) (a, b) (c, d)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_tail
theorems.claim: dropping a head equation decreases (metas, size)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_tail : ∀ (p : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm × NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm) (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns), Prod.Lex (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars U).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize U) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars (p :: U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize (p :: U))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_split
theorems.claim: decomposing two applications decreases (metas, size)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_split : ∀ (f g a b : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm) (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns), Prod.Lex (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U)) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((f.app a, g.app b) :: U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize ((f.app a, g.app b) :: U))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_split_of
theorems.claim: a split head decision decreases (metas, size)
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_split_of : ∀ {s t f g a b : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.split f g a b → Prod.Lex (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize ((f, g) :: (a, b) :: U)) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((s, t) :: U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize ((s, t) :: U))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_bind
theorems.claim: a binding step strictly decreases the number of metas
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.measure_bind : ∀ {s t u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm} {x : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.head s t = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Head.bind x u → Prod.Lex (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) (fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substEqns (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x u) U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.substEqns (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single x u) U)) ((NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnVars ((s, t) :: U)).card, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.eqnSize ((s, t) :: U))

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_complete
theorems.claim: if the equations and solved form have a common unifier some budget answers solved
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_complete : ∀ (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns) (S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm U S → (∃ θ, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U ∧ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ S) → ∃ fuel σ, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U S = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.solved σ

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_succ
theorems.claim: an answer does not change with one more step of budget
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_succ : ∀ (fuel : ℕ) {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {r : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U S = r → r ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.exhausted → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve (fuel + 1) U S = r

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_add
theorems.claim: an answer does not change with any larger budget
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve_add : ∀ {fuel : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {r : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U S = r → r ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.exhausted → ∀ (k : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve (fuel + k) U S = r

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.answers_agree
theorems.claim: two budgets that both answer give the same answer
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.answers_agree : ∀ {f₁ f₂ : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {S : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Solved} {r₁ r₂ : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve f₁ U S = r₁ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve f₂ U S = r₂ → r₁ ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.exhausted → r₂ ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.exhausted → r₁ = r₂

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solvedForm_nil
theorems.claim: a fresh problem is in solved form
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solvedForm_nil : ∀ (U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.SolvedForm U []

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.satisfies_nil
theorems.claim: every substitution satisfies the empty solved form
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.satisfies_nil : ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Satisfies θ []

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solved_mgu
theorems.claim: for a fresh problem an answer solved σ is a most general unifier
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solved_mgu : ∀ {fuel : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {σ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U [] = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.solved σ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies σ U ∧ ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U → ∀ (n : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst θ (σ n) = θ n

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.refused_no_unifier
theorems.claim: for a fresh problem a clash or occurs answer means no unifier exists (invalid-constraint is sound)
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.refused_no_unifier : ∀ {fuel : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U [] = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.clash ∨ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U [] = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.cycle → ∀ (θ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), ¬NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solvable_iff
theorems.claim: the constraints have a unifier exactly when some budget answers solved (fragment completeness)
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solvable_iff : ∀ {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns}, (∃ θ, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ U) ↔ ∃ fuel σ, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U [] = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.solved σ

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.subst_single_sym_ne
theorems.claim: instantiating a meta of a term with two different symbols gives different terms
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.subst_single_sym_ne : ∀ {m : ℕ} {u : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, m ∈ u.vars → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single m (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.sym 0)) u ≠ NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.subst (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.single m (NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm.sym 1)) u

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unique_iff_ground
theorems.claim: all unifiers agree at a meta exactly when the answer is ground there; otherwise two solutions differ (underconstrained is never a silent choice)
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.unique_iff_ground : ∀ {fuel : ℕ} {U : NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Eqns} {σ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm}, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve fuel U [] = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.solved σ → ∀ (n : ℕ), (∀ (θ₁ θ₂ : ℕ → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Tm), NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ₁ U → NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Unifies θ₂ U → θ₁ n = θ₂ n) ↔ (σ n).Ground

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Code.enc_injective
theorems.claim: structural identity of codes is equality of their trees
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Code.enc_injective : Function.Injective NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Code.enc

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Val.enc_injective
theorems.claim: structural identity of values is equality of their trees
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Val.enc_injective : Function.Injective NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Val.enc

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.pairGoal_solved
theorems.claim: Pair ?α I64 against Pair (List Unit) I64 is solved with the ground answer ?α := List Unit
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.pairGoal_solved : ∃ σ, NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.solve 8 NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.pairGoal [] = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Outcome.solved σ ∧ σ 0 = NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.Code.unit.list.enc ∧ (σ 0).Ground

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ImplicitUnification.pairGoal_exhausted
